verdict.reasoning: Patient states, "I've been really stressed at work for the past few days, and I've realized that I've really dry, itchy skin," and later confirms it started "a few days ago."

Location: "All over my arms and my hands, mainly." Symptoms: "really dry, itchy skin" and "my skin's quite red." Timing/trigger: Symptoms started "a few days ago" and when asked, "did your symptoms start after you went swimming?" patient answers "Yes."
Patient explicitly says, "I don't have any spots."
Patient says, "No fever. I'm not sweating either," and later the clinician summarizes, "no fevers."
Patient reports, "I'm using coconut butter for the past few days" and when asked, "the coconut butter hadn't helped with the itch?" responds "No."
When asked, "Do you feel genuinely run down? Do you feel tired?" the patient answers, "Yeah, I think I have been quite tired," consistent with mild fatigue.

Eating/drinking/appetite: "Yeah, I've been drinking and eating as normal. Appetite's fine." Bowels: When asked, "Are your bowels working okay?" patient answers "Yeah," and denies vomiting or loose stools.
When asked, "No fevers, no. Vomiting?" patient replies, "No," and later denies "vomiting or loose stools."

The transcript does not provide a global statement of no past medical or surgical history; the clinician only asks about past skin problems and other medical history generally. Absence of recorded conditions does not equal an explicit "no PMH/PSH."
Patient states, "I'm currently taking microgen," clarified by the clinician as "Microgynal?... It's a contraceptive pill." Patient agrees ("Yeah").
In response to allergy questions, patient says, "I think I might be lactose intolerant."
Family history: patient states, "Yeah, so my dad has asthma..."
Work: "I work as a teacher," and later the clinician confirms, "you said you meant you work as a primary school teacher," patient: "Yes, that's right."
When asked, "who do you live with at home?" patient replies, "It's just me." Clinician clarifies, "Live alone?" and patient answers "Yep."
Smoking: When asked, "do you smoke?" patient replies, "No, I don't smoke."
Alcohol: When asked, "Do you drink much in the way of alcohol?" patient answers, "No," which supports minimal alcohol use.
The clinician asks, "Recreational drugs?" but the transcript does not include the patient's response, so "does not use recreational drugs" is not documented.

Findings: dry, itchy, "quite red" skin on hands/arms, onset a few days after swimming. Clinician summarizes "dry, itchy rash on your... hands... and your arms" and states, "I wonder whether you may have something called dermatitis," consistent with acute pruritic, erythematous dermatitis likely contact/irritant/eczema-type.
Patient reports feeling "quite tired" but otherwise "It's pretty good" health and no systemic symptoms, consistent with mild fatigue in an otherwise well patient.
Clinician: "something called emollients. Which can help with the dry skin. And that's something you just need to kind of paste onto your skin throughout the day for the next few days."
Clinician: "we can readily treat [it] with a couple of options. We have steroid creams I can give you, which will help with inflammation..." indicating prescription/offer of topical corticosteroid.
Clinician: "You can also try antihistamines, so you can get things over the counter. Pyritin, loratadine. That can sometimes help with the itchiness."

While ineffectiveness of coconut butter is discussed, there is no explicit advice to stop using it or to avoid pool exposure/harsh soaps; these avoidance recommendations are not stated in the transcript.
Clinician: "Paracetamol on this occasion wouldn't be helpful. Painkillers wouldn't be helpful on this occasion."
Clinician: "I can give you a patient information lethal [leaflet] about that, which gives a bit more information about the disease."

Clinician: "let's see how the next few days go. And if it's still not getting better, come back and see me next week and we can have another look again at your symptoms." Although earlier return if worsening/systemic symptoms isn't explicitly said, review in about one week if no improvement is clearly advised.
Patient-reported findings: "I've really dry, itchy skin" and "my skin's quite red" on "all over my arms and my hands, mainly," consistent with erythema and pruritus on hands and arms.

The doctor notes, "Normally at this stage I like to proceed examination, but... based on your story, it's difficult," and no vital signs or formal physical examination details are recorded elsewhere in the transcript.
